reproducibility.note: Deterministic metrics give identical results for the same source, rules, tests and tool versions. Readability (LLM) and complexity (timing) can vary slightly between runs.

usefulness.example: 300 submissions for a sorting assignment are compiled, tested and scored overnight; the instructor only reads reports whose grade is incomplete or flagged.
usefulness.benefit: The same rules are applied to every student, and every point lost is explained.

usefulness.example: A student whose sum overflows for INT_MAX + 1 gets that exact input, the expected output and the UBSan message within a minute, and can resubmit.
usefulness.benefit: Concrete counter-examples teach more than a bare score.

usefulness.example: Two submissions with renamed variables reach similarity 0.93 against a 0.85 threshold and are flagged; the instructor checks only those pairs.
usefulness.benefit: Review time goes to the suspicious cases only, and no one is penalised automatically.

usefulness.example: Candidates are ranked by correctness, edge cases and memory safety, with a per-metric explanation for every rejection.

limitations.example: A program that special-cases the exact hidden inputs passes every test and still gets full correctness marks.
limitations.mitigation: Upload a reference solution so random counter-tests are compared against it.

limitations.limitation: LLM-written expected outputs can be wrong
limitations.example: The model claims the digit sum of -1234 is -10; a correct program printing 10 fails that test.
limitations.mitigation: The teacher review step before Accept; edit or regenerate doubtful tests.

limitations.example: An O(n log n) sort and an O(n) loop can produce the same curve at n <= 32000 when input reading dominates, so both are reported as O(n).
limitations.mitigation: Use larger sizes in the rules; the report gives the fit quality and a confidence level.

limitations.limitation: Similarity misses rewritten copies and over-flags tiny programs
limitations.example: An LLM answer rewritten with a different loop structure scores 0.4 and is not flagged, while two honest 6-line add-two-numbers programs look identical.
limitations.mitigation: Flags are only review requests; short programs are never flagged.
